headline: One transaction is over-credited by exactly 1 point with no rounding involved, but the gold does not dispute it, so an agent that disputes every discrepancy fails.

issues.summary: Under the documented rates and floor rounding, three of Kenji's five transactions mismatch: the two gold disputes (under-credited) and txn_31fd03682992, which is over-credited by 1 point (289.50 x 4% = 1158.00 exactly, stored 1159). The gold leaves the over-credit undisputed; nothing in the KB says to skip overpayments or tiny discrepancies.
evidence: db.json credit_card_transaction_history[txn_31fd03682992]: Hilton Seattle, Travel, $289.50, rewards_earned "1159 points"
doc_credit_cards_silver_rewards_card_002: "Pay with your card for eligible travel and software transactions to earn 4.0% back"
Computation: 289.50 x 4.0 = 1158.00 points (no fractional part, so floor and round-half-up both give 1158) vs stored 1159

doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_003: "Use this process when a customer believes there is a discrepancy between the cash back they received for a particular transaction and the cash back they should have received."
gold[2..3] dispute only txn_cfabb609133d (87.25 x 1% = 87, stored 47) and txn_913d14a20dc5 (156.78 x 1% = 156.78 -> 156, stored 15)
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that treats any discrepancy as an error (the reading task_018/022 explicitly reward for over-credits) hands the user a third dispute; the extra cash_back_disputes and user_discoverable_tool_calls rows break the DB hash. Only an agent that chooses to ignore a 1-point over-credit in the customer's favour matches.
issues.suggested_fix: Set txn_31fd03682992.rewards_earned to "1158 points" in db.json, or add it to the gold dispute set.

issues.summary: The floor-rounding rule that makes the gold dispute set exact (doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007) is not in this task's required_documents, so the golden_retrieval variant never shows it.
evidence: task_017.required_documents does not include doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007 (grep: only task_028 lists it)
src/tau2/domains/banking_knowledge/retrieval.py build_tools: "# No retrieval tools (no_knowledge, full_kb, golden_retrieval)"

doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007: "All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number. When calculating points earned on a purchase, the system always truncates (floors) fractional points rather than rounding to the nearest integer."
issues.why_it_matters: Under golden_retrieval the agent cannot search the KB, so it must guess the rounding convention; round-half-up also flags txn_cedd88ce1f65 (54.99 x 4% = 219.96 -> 220 vs stored 219) on top of the txn_31fd03682992 problem. Search-based configs (default alltools, bm25, etc.) can retrieve doc_007, so headline scores are unaffected.

solution_check: Computed all 5 Silver Rewards transactions with 4% Travel/Software, 1% otherwise, floored per doc_..._(general)_007: e4ed366 1800=1800, 913d14 156 vs 15, 31fd03 1158 vs 1159, cfabb6 87 vs 47, cedd88 219 (219.96) = 219. Floor gives {913d14, cfabb6, 31fd03}; round-half-up gives those plus cedd88. Gold is {913d14, cfabb6}: it matches only if the agent drops the 1-point over-credit.
prior_note: Prior (Major) blamed undocumented rounding; rounding is documented (doc_007 is unchanged since v1.0.0) and resolves cedd88, but the 31fd03 off-by-one is independent of rounding and keeps the task Major.
notes: txn_913d14a20dc5 also has an unrelated transaction_disputes row (duplicate_charge, UNDER_REVIEW); it does not affect cash-back grading. A prior verification_history row for Kenji (11/10/2025) exists; the new log uses a different id (time-based).
